newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan Phosphate seeks $170 mln for growth.
newsitem.headline: Jordan Phosphate seeks $170 mln for growth.

text.p: Jordan Phosphate Mines Company has gained shareholder approval to seek $170 million in foreign and local funding for ambitious expansion projects.

Shareholders at an extraordinary AGM on Tuesday approved the board's request to access funding from foreign and domestic financial institutions for a $250 million expansion project at the firm's Shidiyah mine.
Sameh Madani, general manager, said the company had planned to tap global cpaital markets for $100 million with another 50 million dinars ($70,620) from local financing.
But the company was still mulling whether the $100 million should be secured through a bond issue or through a GDR (Global Depository Receipt) listing.
A $25 million bridging loan from local banks will be negotiated soon for immediate needs, Madani said.

Madani said the company's decision to proceed quickly on the Shidiyah project was prompted by improved world demand and likely extra demand from Jordan's own downstream fertilizer joint venture projects.

The project will more than double production to around eight million tonnes by 1998 from the Shidiyah mine, which with its high grade phosphate, is by far the lowest cost producer of Jordan's three operating mines. It holds one billion of Jordan's 1.5 billion tonnes of proven reserves.

The company's total sales rose to 254.4 million dinars in 1996 from 226.1 million dinars in 1995, Madani said. Its pre-tax profits rose to 27.7 million dinars at end of 1996 from 15.5 million in 1995.

Two major projects are expected to come on stream in the second quarter of this year: a $170 million plant to export phosphoric acid to a fertilizer complex in India and a second $85 million Japanese-Jordanian project to produce ammonium phosphates and compound fertiliser.
The company which has a a majority state ownership exceeding 80 percent also has a significant 16.28 stake held by Kuwait.
